title: Conjugate acid-base partition
statement: A conjugate acid/base relation is a pair of retained chemical identities differing by exactly one named proton carrier: the protonated member donates it and the deprotonated member accepts it.
generation_rule: Generate the literal product of the registered conjugate pair, carrier, acid role, base role, difference, orientation, record and extension choices.
grammar_boundary: Every finite generated pair of chemical carriers related by exactly one retained proton occurrence, with the protonated member able to donate that occurrence and the deprotonated member able to accept it.

choices.name: one-species-label
choices.reason: A conjugate relation compares two carrier identities.

choices.name: two-conjugate-identities
choices.reason: Both protonated and deprotonated carriers remain held.

choices.name: anonymous-hydrogen-count
choices.reason: A count cannot trace the transferred occurrence.

choices.name: one-held-proton-occurrence
choices.reason: The distinguishing proton remains a named conserved carrier.

choices.name: acid-by-name
choices.reason: A name cannot establish a transition.

choices.name: proton-donor-role
choices.reason: The protonated carrier supplies the held proton to an acceptor.

choices.name: base-by-name
choices.reason: A name cannot establish a transition.

choices.name: proton-acceptor-role
choices.reason: The deprotonated carrier accepts the held proton.

choices.name: differ-by-one-proton
choices.reason: All other retained composition is identical.

choices.name: signed-acidity-scalar
choices.reason: A signed scalar is not a carrier trace.

choices.name: held-donor-acceptor-orientation
choices.reason: Roles are structural orientations on one transfer.

choices.name: pair-and-proton-trace
choices.reason: Both identities, the proton and transition remain held.

choices.name: free-acid-base-exception
choices.reason: An exception can label arbitrary species.

choices.name: no-extra-rule
choices.reason: One-proton conjugacy and roles determine the relation.

induction_base: One retained carrier pair differing by one named proton supplies the first conjugate acid/base relation.
induction_step: Appending matched retained composition to both members preserves their one-proton difference and donor/acceptor orientation.
exclusions: no acid/base dictionary, pH scale, equilibrium equation, dissociation constant, measured value or V2 answer may select a candidate
no numerical zero, negative, irrational, imaginary or floating proof quantity
no free, fitted, learned or target-derived parameter
no unpaired creation, copying or loss of a proton or electron carrier
no claim that structural closure alone fixes every solution-dependent strength or capacity value
external target content remains inaccessible until the prediction is sealed

Every finite generated pair of chemical carriers related by exactly one retained proton occurrence, with the protonated member able to donate that occurrence and the deprotonated member able to accept it.
operational_witnesses: the two conjugate identities remain distinct
the distinguishing carrier is explicitly proton-labelled

target_rows.source_locator: official IUPAC source set anchored at C01266

falsification_condition: The claim fails if the authoritative conjugate acid/base record lacks proton donation, proton acceptance or a one-proton conjugate relation, or if a changed row is accepted.
